v1.feedback: The Shiota-web-meets-Möbius concept lands: red threads converging on a suspended sphere is immediately readable, and the periodic twist event where threads warp and palette flips red→teal is a genuine surprise, not a rename. Two things to fix: the wireframe Möbius band overlay is didactic — lose it and let the threads themselves trace the half-twist topology so the form is discovered, not annotated. Second, 20k segments at opacity 0.07 with additive blending risk reading as a diffuse red fog rather than distinct threads at typical screen distance; drop count to ~8k and raise per-line opacity to 0.14–0.18 so individual filaments remain legible, which is the whole point of a Shiota reference.

v2.feedback: The Möbius half-twist wave is a real topological idea encoded in the thread mechanics, not just a label — good. However, at opacity 0.16 with additive blending the filaments may be too faint to read as a coherent Shiota web in under 2 seconds; bump base opacity to ~0.22–0.28 or add a second pass with thicker highlight lines for the sphere-convergent category. The 28-second twist period means a casual viewer likely misses the signature effect entirely — shorten TWIST_PERIOD to ~12s or start the first twist at t=3s so the Möbius idea lands immediately. The teal color shift is the strongest moment; consider letting a faint teal residue linger (~10% blend) after each twist so the piece accumulates visual history rather than fully resetting to monochrome red.
